doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Drum and bugle corps and composing marches with Paul Morrison
summary: Drum and bugle corps from age twelve and high school band director Paul Morrison's harmony class, which led to two band marches.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Morrison, and I was exposed through his tutoring also to composition. After school he would gather us together, a few of the most promising students in music and conduct a harmony class. So he would teach us how to write music, of course teaching the chords and everything that you would eventually need to know to like compose a march — and that was our first project, was to write a march that you would play in the band, the concert band. So after some of his training, I started writing some pieces. And I wrote two band marches and I found out not too long ago that those two band marches are still in the library—

And as a matter of fact I think it was about twenty years ago, they invited me back to conduct one of the numbers, just a guest conductor. And they chose one of my compositions. And I wrote the first one when I was sixteen years old, and the second one a year later. And I had started to write an overture by the time that I was ready to be graduated from school. I never quite finished that one.
Well Schubert has his Unfinished Symphony. I have my Unfinished Overture.
